## What Is Webinar Software and How is it Used for Virtual Events?


Webinar software is a digital platform that supports live, interactive online presentations, seminars, or events. It enables hosts to broadcast audio, video, and multimedia content to a remote audience in real time.


These platforms typically offer tools for screen sharing, chat, polls, and Q&A, allowing for two-way communication between presenters and attendees. Webinar software is used across industries for training, marketing, product demonstrations, and internal communications.


Webinar software helps organizations run virtual events without the location, capacity, and travel limits of in-person sessions. It also provides tools for managing attendees, encouraging participation, and measuring event performance from a single platform.


**Key benefits of these platforms for virtual events:**


- **Reach a wider audience:** Attendees can join from different locations using an internet-connected device, making webinars suitable for regional and global audiences.
- **Reduce event costs:** Virtual events can reduce spending on venues, travel, accommodation, catering, and printed materials.
- **Improve audience engagement:** Features such as live chat, polls, Q&A, and surveys allow attendees to interact with presenters during the event.
- **Simplify event management:** Registration pages, automated reminders, attendee tracking, and follow-up emails help reduce manual administrative work.
- **Measure event performance:** Analytics can show registrations, attendance rates, viewing time, engagement, and other data that helps teams evaluate results.
- **Reuse webinar content:** Recorded sessions can be shared on demand, used for internal training, or repurposed into other marketing and educational content.
- **Connect with other business tools:** Integrations with CRM, email marketing, and automation platforms can help synchronize attendee data and support follow-up workflows.

## Types of Virtual Events You Can Host with Webinar Software


### 1. Virtual Conferences


[Virtual conferences](https://corp.kaltura.com/blog/virtual-conference-platform/) use webinar software to bring together large groups of attendees for multi-session events. These platforms support multiple tracks, breakout rooms, and keynote presentations, allowing for a comprehensive conference experience. Organizers can:


- Invite speakers from around the world
- Schedule simultaneous sessions
- Enable networking through chat or virtual meeting spaces


This format is suitable for industry summits, academic gatherings, or annual meetings that require broad participation and diverse content. A major advantage of virtual conferences is accessibility. Attendees avoid travel costs and can participate from their own devices, which often leads to higher turnout. Organizers can record sessions for on-demand access, making content available to those who miss live presentations. Webinar software’s engagement features, such as polls and Q&A, foster interaction despite the remote setting.


### 2. Product Demonstrations


Product demonstrations leverage webinar software to showcase products to potential customers, partners, or internal teams. Presenters can:


- Share their screens
- Display product features in real time
- Answer questions instantly


This approach allows businesses to reach a wider audience, including prospects who may not be able to attend in-person demonstrations due to distance or scheduling conflicts. Webinar software also enables interactive demos, where attendees can participate in live polls, chat with presenters, or request feature walkthroughs. The ability to record sessions and provide on-demand access means prospects can revisit demonstrations at their convenience.


### 3. Virtual Training Sessions


Organizations use webinar software for virtual training sessions to educate employees, partners, or customers on products, processes, or compliance topics. Trainers can:


- Deliver presentations
- Share documents
- Conduct real-time assessments using quizzes or polls


This format is useful for onboarding new hires, rolling out new software, or delivering ongoing professional development. The interactive features of webinar software, such as breakout rooms and live Q&A, enhance the learning experience by allowing participants to ask questions and collaborate in smaller groups. Trainers can track attendance and engagement metrics to ensure knowledge retention and identify areas needing further attention.


### 4. Marketing and Lead Generation Webinars


Marketing teams use webinar software to host webinars aimed at generating leads and nurturing prospects. These events typically focus on thought leadership, industry trends, or educational content relevant to the target audience. Attendees register in advance, providing valuable contact information for follow-up campaigns. Elements that increase engagement and help qualify leads based on participation include:


- Live polls
- Q&A
- Interactive content


Webinar software integrates with marketing automation and CRM platforms, simplifying the process of capturing, scoring, and nurturing leads. Post-webinar analytics reveal which topics and presenters resonate most, guiding future marketing efforts.


### 5. Company Town Halls


[Company town halls](https://corp.kaltura.com/blog/what-is-a-town-hall-meeting/) conducted via webinar software enable organizations to communicate important updates, share strategic goals, and celebrate achievements with their entire workforce. Executives can:


- Address employees directly
- Provide clarity on organizational changes
- Foster a sense of unity, regardless of where employees are located


Features like live Q&A and chat encourage participation and feedback. Using webinar software for town halls ensures that all employees, including remote or distributed teams, receive consistent messaging. Recordings allow those who miss the live session to catch up later, ensuring transparency and inclusion. The platform’s reporting tools help measure engagement and gather employee sentiment.


## What to Look for in Webinar Software for Virtual Events


### Attendee Capacity


The attendee capacity of webinar software determines the maximum number of participants who can join a session. Different platforms offer varying capacity limits, from small group meetings to large-scale events with thousands of attendees. Choosing software with the right capacity ensures a smooth experience for all participants and prevents disruptions due to system overloads or access restrictions.


When evaluating webinar solutions, **consider** both your current and anticipated audience sizes. Some platforms allow you to scale up as your event grows, while others may charge additional fees for increased capacity. It’s important to understand these limitations and costs upfront to avoid issues during high-demand events. Adequate capacity is critical for hosting successful virtual conferences, product launches, or company-wide meetings.


### Live Streaming and Video Quality


High-quality live streaming is essential for maintaining audience engagement and delivering a professional event experience. Webinar software should support HD video, clear audio, and minimal latency to ensure presentations are smooth and uninterrupted. Poor video quality or frequent buffering can diminish the credibility of your event and frustrate attendees, leading to lower satisfaction and engagement rates.


**Look for** platforms that adapt streaming quality based on attendees’ internet connections and provide backup options for presenters. Some software includes features like virtual backgrounds, noise suppression, or presenter spotlighting to enhance the viewing experience. Reliable streaming technology is especially important for large events or sessions with multiple speakers, where seamless transitions and consistent quality are crucial.


### Audience Engagement Features


Engagement features such as live polls, Q&A, chat, and reactions help keep attendees involved and attentive during virtual events. These tools enable two-way communication, allowing participants to ask questions, provide feedback, or interact with presenters in real time. Active engagement leads to a more dynamic and memorable event, increasing the likelihood of knowledge retention and positive outcomes.


The best webinar software provides flexible engagement options that can be tailored to different event formats. For example, breakout rooms encourage small group discussions during training sessions, while polls can be used to gauge audience sentiment during conferences. Analytics on engagement activities help organizers identify which sessions or topics generated the most interest, informing future event planning.


### Registration and Event Management


Effective registration and event management tools simplify the attendee experience from sign-up to post-event follow-up. Webinar software should support customizable registration forms, automated confirmation emails, and calendar integrations to reduce manual administrative work. These features ensure that attendees receive timely reminders and easy access to event details, minimizing no-shows and technical issues.


Event management capabilities often include attendee tracking, waitlist management, and integration with CRM or marketing platforms. This allows organizers to monitor sign-ups, segment audiences, and personalize communications. Smooth registration and management processes contribute to higher attendance rates and a more professional image for your virtual events.

### Recording and On-Demand Webinars


Recording functionality allows you to capture live sessions and make them available for on-demand viewing. This is valuable for attendees who cannot join the live event or wish to revisit key segments. On-demand webinars extend the reach of your content, providing ongoing value and enabling organizations to build a library of educational or promotional materials.


**Look for** webinar software that offers easy recording controls, cloud storage, and options to edit or share recordings securely. Some platforms enable you to gate access to on-demand content, capturing additional leads or tracking viewer engagement. Providing recordings helps maximize the impact of your events and ensures that important information remains accessible over time.


### Analytics and Reporting


Comprehensive analytics and reporting tools are essential for measuring the success of your virtual events. Webinar software should track metrics such as registration numbers, attendance rates, engagement levels, and post-event feedback. These insights help organizers understand what worked well and where improvements are needed, guiding future event strategy.


Advanced reporting features may include heatmaps of engagement, detailed breakdowns of poll or Q&A participation, and integration with external analytics platforms. Access to real-time and post-event data enables organizations to optimize content, target follow-up communications, and demonstrate ROI to stakeholders.


## Notable Webinar Software for Virtual Events


**How we selected these tools:** We shortlisted webinar software for virtual events based on the session formats each platform supports, attendee capacity and streaming delivery, audience engagement features, registration and event management, recording and on-demand distribution, and analytics and CRM integration.


### Enterprise Webinar and Virtual Event Platforms


#### 1. Kaltura Webinars


**Best for:** Marketing teams running branded, data-driven webinar programs


**Strengths:** AI engagement assistant, gamification, cross-webinar analytics


**Things to consider:** Advanced setup and feature breadth take time to learn


Kaltura Webinars handles live broadcasts, simulive events, breakout rooms, and on-demand recordings from a single interface. The same hub is used to schedule sessions, stream them, and measure them, and recorded sessions convert into on-demand content automatically.


Alongside delivery, the platform includes a content lab for turning session footage into clips and galleries, and marketing automation integrations that pass registration and engagement data into systems such as Marketo, HubSpot, Eloqua, and Pardot.


**Key features include:**


- **All-in-one session hub:** Supports live broadcasts, simulive events, breakout rooms, and on-demand recordings from one interface, with single sign-on for access control.
- **AI-generated event sites:** A generative AI content and agenda builder creates a branded landing page or event site from images, headshots, and event details, and also generates the webinar title and email templates.
- **Real-time engagement suite:** Live and scheduled polls, group chat and 1:1 networking, session moderation and Q&A, real-time notifications and announcements, a full set of gamification tools, an engagement leaderboard, and certifications and badges.
- **AI assistant and sentiment analysis:** A real-time, data-based AI assistant indicates where and how to lift audience engagement, and a sentiment analyzer reads the room during the session.
- **First-party analytics and lead scoring:** Tracks participant interactions, focus rates, and performance metrics in real time, with advanced cross-webinar analytics and lead scoring reports that integrate with marketing automation platforms.
- **Content repurposing and on-demand delivery:** A video content lab consolidates recordings, adds VOD in advance and ASR captioning, chapterizes content, and edits sessions into shareable clips and galleries, with AI-generated follow-up emails and on-demand links.
- **Promotion and distribution:** Branded site and landing page generation, an embedded webinar calendar, and sharing or broadcasting across social channels.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/kaltura-video-cloud/reviews) **):**


- **Setup of advanced options:** Some reviewers note that configuring more advanced elements, such as complex registration forms, takes longer than the rest of the setup.
- **Initial learning curve:** The breadth of features can feel like a lot to take in during the first sessions, though reviewers point to support as helping bridge that.
- **Marketing reporting gaps:** A few users wanted more marketing-side reporting, such as UTM attribution, alongside the engagement analytics.


Source:[Kaltura](https://corp.kaltura.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Message-Page@2x.png)


#### 2. ON24


**Best for:** Enterprise B2B webinar programs tied to CRM and MAP data


**Strengths:** Personalization, 20+ engagement tools, deep webcast analytics


**Things to consider:** Steep learning curve, backend feels dated to new users


ON24, a Cvent company, runs live, simulive, pre-recorded, and on-demand webinars from one platform. Setup uses event templates, drag-and-drop registration pages, a dedicated speaker green room, and a production studio, and scales from small roundtables to series with thousands of attendees.


Each webinar can be tailored per attendee, with messaging, surveys, and calls-to-action varying by segment. Engagement data feeds in real time into marketing automation platforms and CRMs so sales and marketing teams work from the same signals.


**Key features include:**


- **Multiple webinar formats:** Live, simulive with pre-recorded content scheduled to play at a set time while presenters handle live Q&A, sim-2-live rollover into a live segment, and on-demand; live and simulive sessions switch to on-demand at the same audience URL.
- **Builder tools for event setup:** A drag-and-drop registration builder, an email builder for promotion and follow-up, a segment builder for audience targeting, and a console builder controlling layouts, colors, and backgrounds.
- **Engagement and conversion tools:** Over 20 tools including real-time Q&A, live polls and surveys, chat, downloadable resources, personalized calls-to-action, and breakout rooms.
- **Captioning and translation:** Automated live captioning in English plus six other Western European languages, automated on-demand transcripts in 15+ languages with translation into 60+, human live captioning and subtitles in 100+ languages, and live audio interpretation.
- **Webcast analytics:** Real-time attendee engagement metrics, detailed audience reports, attendance rates, interaction levels, content engagement, and AI-identified key moments, with interaction-based heat maps that generate video clips.
- **AI content repurposing:** ACE, the analytics and content engine, generates transcripts, blogs, and highlights from recorded sessions, and AI-powered nurture pages target registrants who did not attend.
- **Integrations and distribution:** Native connections to Salesforce, Marketo, and Google Analytics, plus content hubs, virtual events with breakout sessions and networking lounges, and gamified virtual conferences.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/on24/reviews) **):**


- **Learning curve:** Reviewers describe a steep learning curve when setting up events and configuring widgets, with new hosts often needing training first.
- **Backend interface:** Several users find the webinar builder interface dated and less intuitive than newer platforms.
- **Customization limits:** Reports of constrained options for registration page layout, console branding, and visual page adjustments.
- **Cost and tiered features:** Users mention high pricing and capabilities that sit behind higher tiers or additional charges.
- **Performance with large audiences:** Some report the system feels sluggish when managing large numbers of registrants and guests.


Source:[ON24](https://www.on24.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Screenshot-2026-02-24-at-7.30.15-PM-1024x641.png)


#### 3. BigMarker


**Best for:** Marketers who need heavy branding control over webinars


**Strengths:** 200+ features, browser-based delivery, wide CRM integrations


**Things to consider:** Many settings to configure, occasional platform glitches


BigMarker runs webinars in the browser with no downloads for attendees, and lists over 200 features spanning delivery, promotion, and reporting. Hosts present from the built-in studio or stream in over RTMP, and can run sessions live, prerecorded as simulive, recurring, or on demand.


Landing pages, email invitations, and reminders are bundled with the webinar itself, and data captured through forms, polls, Q&A, and offers is pushed into CRM and marketing automation systems. Enterprise plans scale to 50,000 attendees.


**Key features include:**


- **Multiple webinar formats and capacity:** Unlimited live, recurring, automated simulive, and on-demand webinars, with plans supporting audiences up to 50,000 attendees.
- **Browser-based room with branding control:** Runs in the cloud through a web browser with no attendee downloads, supports HD audio and video with up to 64 people on camera at once, HD screen sharing, and logo and theme color customization.
- **Built-in promotion and registration:** 15+ landing page templates, customizable invites and reminder sequences, and embeddable registration forms, live webinars, and on-demand videos for a company website.
- **Audience interaction tools:** Public and private chat, Q&A with upvoting so top questions rise, polls and quizzes, offer and call-to-action pop-ups, breakout rooms, downloadable resources, and the ability to bring any attendee on screen.
- **Presentation and streaming controls:** Preload presentations or add files in-room, play and pause YouTube and MP4 videos for all viewers, whiteboard mark-up, no presenter limit, dial-in telephony, and simulcasting to Facebook and YouTube Live.
- **Analytics and integrations:** Click-level tracking of attendee engagement, analytics dashboards and reports, and native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, Marketo, Pardot, and Eloqua.
- **Monetization and compliance extras:** Sponsor banners for selling event sponsorships, and attendance certificates that track CEU requirements.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/bigmarker/reviews) **):**


- **Volume of settings:** Reviewers repeatedly note that the number of options in event creation can be overwhelming and slows down setup.
- **Branding and layout flexibility:** Users report limits on customizing page templates and layouts independently, sometimes needing vendor assistance.
- **Third-party integrations:** Some describe friction with CRM syncing and gaps in coverage for certain platforms, affecting post-event workflows.
- **Occasional glitches:** A number of users describe bugs and audio or recording issues that appeared during live sessions.
- **Recording output:** Recordings are delivered as a single master file rather than separate audio and video tracks per presenter, which limits editing flexibility.


Source:[BigMarker](https://www.bigmarker.com/assets/home/new_feature_pages/webinars_hero-img.png)


#### 4. Webex Webinars


**Best for:** Large global webinars needing multilingual accessibility


**Strengths:** Up to 100,000 attendees, live translation, rehearsal tools


**Things to consider:** Limited branding options, busy host interface


Webex Webinars, formerly Webex Events, is Cisco’s webinar workflow within the Webex Suite. It handles sessions from small groups up to 100,000 attendees, covering registration, moderation, and post-event controls in one place.


Hosts get rehearsal and stage management features to prepare before going live and to control what the audience sees before, during, and after the session. The platform integrates with Slido and Miro, and Cisco offers a production services team for event support.


**Key features include:**


- **Large-scale audience reach:** Accommodates up to 100,000 attendees, with real-time translations available in over 100 languages.
- **Registration and branding:** Custom branding options and themes shape the attendee registration experience for each event.
- **Rehearsal and stage management:** Presenters rehearse the full presentation with co-panelists before going live, and hosts direct the stage and the content the audience sees at each phase of the event.
- **Audience engagement:** Moderated Q&A, live polling, chat, emoji reactions, and gesture recognition, with Slido adding six polling types and additional Q&A.
- **Breakout sessions:** Attendees split into smaller groups to explore topics in depth or interact more directly with panelists.
- **Accessibility:** Live interpreters are included in session so attendees can listen to the event in their preferred language.
- **Presentation tools:** Immersive share places the presenter directly on top of the shared content, and the platform integrates with everyday tools including Miro and Slido.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/webex-events-webinars/reviews) **):**


- **Customization limits:** The most common criticism is restricted branding and layout control, including design elements that cannot be changed.
- **Learning curve:** Reviewers describe the backend as confusing for first-time hosts, with advanced settings buried in menus after updates.
- **Setup effort for complex events:** Registration forms, panelist management, and multi-session events are reported as time-consuming to configure.
- **Performance demands:** Some users find the client heavy on older devices or limited bandwidth, and report slow report generation on large data sets.
- **Interface age:** Several reviewers say the interface feels dated relative to newer webinar platforms.


Source:[Webex](https://cisco-api.ingeniuxondemand.com/DITA/content/en/us/td/i/400001-500000/450001-460000/457001-458000/457748.jpg)


### Business and Marketing Webinar Software


#### 5. Zoom Webinars


**Best for:** Teams that want a familiar interface and fast setup


**Strengths:** Scales to 100,000, Production Studio, Simulive, AI captions


**Things to consider:** Layered backend setup, limited branding flexibility


Zoom’s webinar software covers one-time webinars, recurring series, and multi-session conferences from one platform, scaling from ten attendees up to 100,000. Zoom reports over 9 million webinars and 692 million webinar attendees annually based on its 2025 internal data.


Production Studio handles custom layouts, pre-loaded video, and scene switching, while Simulive allows teams to pre-record a session, broadcast it as live, and step in at the end for Q&A. A private backstage area lets hosts manage speakers and resolve issues mid-event.


**Key features include:**


- **Multiple event formats at scale:** One-time webinars, recurring series, multi-session conferences, virtual events with lobbies, expo floors and networking hubs, and hybrid events with mobile chat and on-screen video for remote attendees.
- **Production tools:** Production Studio for custom layouts, pre-loaded videos and scene switching, a private virtual backstage for coordinating speakers, and isolated per-participant audio and video recording that imports into Premiere, Final Cut Pro, or DaVinci Resolve.
- **Simulive and restreaming:** Pre-record webinars to run as live events, and broadcast simultaneously to YouTube, LinkedIn, and Facebook over RTMP while retaining production control inside Zoom.
- **Audience engagement:** Branded registration pages, immersive event lobbies, real-time polls, Q&A, chat, reactions, breakout rooms, and AI-powered captions in more than 20 languages.
- **On-demand and content repurposing:** Branded video hubs for recordings, AI-generated chapters and highlights for navigating long sessions, auto-generated social posts and promotional assets, and engagement tracking on on-demand views.
- **Analytics and CRM connection:** Interactive dashboards for sorting and filtering attendee and engagement data across multiple events, at-a-glance metrics identifying the most engaged participants, and participant data connected directly to a CRM.
- **Training and certification:** Set completion requirements for live training sessions and issue certificates automatically when participants meet them.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-events-and-webinars/reviews) **):**


- **Pricing at scale:** Reviewers commonly cite cost for larger attendee tiers as a constraint for smaller organizations.
- **Backend navigation:** Users describe the event setup flow as layered and clunky, with extra clicks needed for small changes.
- **Branding flexibility:** Several reviewers report limited visual customization of the live event experience and registration assets.
- **Analytics depth:** Some report that reporting and post-event analytics do not go as deep as they need for attendee insight.
- **Multi-session setup:** Configuring ticketing, session linking, and speaker access for multi-day events is described as time-consuming.


Source:[Zoom](https://news.zoom.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Zoom-Single-Use-Webinar-1M.png)


#### 6. GoTo Webinar


**Best for:** Straightforward marketing, training, and campus webinars


**Strengths:** Quick setup, Practice Mode, Simulive, CRM integrations


**Things to consider:** Dated interface, key features limited to higher tiers


GoTo Webinar is an all-in-one webinar platform used for marketing keynotes, employee training, and campus-wide events, and GoTo reports it powers over 2.8 million events per year. Scheduling, registration, delivery, and follow-up all run through a single dashboard.


Features are organized around the event lifecycle: building and promoting the event beforehand, engaging attendees during the session, and reporting afterwards. Plans are tiered as Reach, Elevate, and Unlimited, with feature availability varying between them.


**Key features include:**


- **Scheduling and rehearsal:** Webinars are scheduled from an intuitive dashboard, and Practice Mode lets presenters rehearse the session before going live.
- **Registration and promotion:** Custom branded registration pages and forms capture lead data, with customizable email invitations, confirmations, and reminders, plus payment collection for paid events and certifications.
- **Simulive events:** Content can be pre-recorded and combined with prepared polls and Q&A to run as a scheduled interactive session.
- **Engagement toolkit:** Interactive polls, live Q&A, and breakout rooms during the session, with closed captioning and screen reader support for accessible delivery.
- **Analytics and reporting:** Post-session reports track attendance and measure engagement, and integrations extend that into a fuller view of the attendee journey.
- **Integrations:** Connects with HubSpot, Marketo, Salesforce Pardot, Prezi, Intellum, and Interprefy to sync registrant data and manage the event from one place.
- **Security and scale:** Enterprise-grade security, data privacy, session encryption, secure logins, and GDPR compliance across events from small trainings to global conferences.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/goto-webinar/reviews) **):**


- **Feature depth:** Reviewers describe the feature set as basic compared with newer platforms, with limited customization and flexibility.
- **Pricing tiers:** Capabilities such as cloud recording, registrant imports, and multi-session registration are reported as reserved for higher plans.
- **Interface age:** Several users call the interface dated and clunky, particularly when switching between screen share and webcam mid-session.
- **App download:** Some attendees are reported to need an application download rather than joining entirely in the browser.
- **Support experience:** Multiple reviewers describe slow or unhelpful customer support, particularly for accounts on monthly plans.
- **Technical reliability:** Users report intermittent audio, webcam, and screen sharing problems during live sessions.


Source:[GoTo](https://ca.v-cdn.net/6038716/uploads/XELOK3DMO667/screenshot-2026-05-08-095239.png)


#### 7. Livestorm


**Best for:** Marketing teams running browser-based webinars and demos


**Strengths:** No-download attendance, email cadences, CRM sync, analytics


**Things to consider:** Limited branding depth, pricing rises with volume


Livestorm is a browser-based platform covering live webinars, on-demand and automated webinars, virtual events, and restreaming to multiple destinations at once. Attendees connect directly from a browser without installing software, which removes a common source of drop-off.


Setup runs through registration pages, email cadences, and event room branding, with reporting built into the same dashboard. Livestorm states that more than 5,000 organizations use the platform to host their online events.


**Key features include:**


- **Multiple webinar formats:** Live webinars, on-demand webinars created without an expiration date, fully automated webinars driven by preset workflows, virtual events, and restreaming to several platforms simultaneously.
- **Registration and promotion:** Customizable registration pages, custom registration and participation fields for collecting data, email cadences with unlimited reminders and follow-ups using templates, text, or custom HTML, and embeddable website widgets and registration forms.
- **Branding:** Custom asset branding across registration pages, emails, and the event room, plus custom room design with logo, background images, and colors for each event.
- **Engagement features:** Fully customizable polls with results visible in real time, a centralized questions and answers tab in the event room, emoji reactions, and file sharing during the session.
- **Reporting:** An integrated dashboard covering registrations, attendance rate, participation reports, replay analytics, and a contacts record where all contact data can be viewed and exported from one place.
- **Integrations:** Native connections to Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and Pardot, plus Zapier and an app marketplace with thousands of integrations.
- **Accessibility:** AI-powered real-time translated subtitles let attendees follow a live event in their preferred language.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/livestorm/reviews) **):**


- **Branding and layout constraints:** The most frequently cited issue is limited customization of registration pages, emails, and layouts, with several options tied to higher-tier plans.
- **Pricing for smaller teams:** Reviewers describe the cost as steep as attendee volumes and advanced feature needs grow.
- **Analytics depth:** Users want deeper engagement metrics and more flexible export and segmentation of event data.
- **Form logic:** Registration forms are reported to lack conditional fields and custom validation rules for tailored lead capture.
- **Performance on large events:** Occasional lag, delays, and disconnections are reported during larger sessions or on weaker connections.


Source:[Livestorm](https://www.datocms-assets.com/1127/1673447023-livestorm-transcript.png?h=auto&w=840&fm=png&auto=format&q=30&dpr=2)


#### 8. Demio


**Best for:** Small marketing teams running lead-gen webinars and demos


**Strengths:** Simple browser-based setup, engagement analytics, automation


**Things to consider:** Basic feature set, reported streaming reliability issues


Demio, part of the Banzai family, is a browser-based webinar platform used by marketing, sales, and customer success teams. It supports live webinars, product demos, on-demand and automated webinars, and virtual events.


In-session engagement tools are paired with reporting that identifies which attendees interacted with polls, handouts, and calls-to-action, and that data can be merged into a marketing automation platform or CRM for follow-up.


**Key features include:**


- **Live, automated, and on-demand webinars:** Events run live or on autopilot through automated and on-demand sessions that continue to generate registrations outside working hours.
- **Engagement tools:** Real-time chat with question tagging into a dedicated Q&A, emojis and @ mentions to drive conversation, polls for live feedback, downloadable resources for attendees, and featured actions that direct attendees to a call-to-action.
- **Presentation and stage controls:** Slides and videos are uploaded ahead of the session or the screen is shared instead, guest presenters and moderators can be added to manage chat and materials, and attendees can be brought to the stage during a live webinar.
- **Registration and branding:** Custom registration fields capture information from new leads, registrants can be redirected automatically to a chosen URL, and logo and color palette apply across the registration page, email notifications, and webinar room, with branded virtual backgrounds for presenters.
- **Insights and people reports:** The insights report shows registrants over time, who attended and who missed, who was most focused, where people dropped off, and who downloaded handouts, answered polls, or clicked featured actions; the people report segments contacts by attendance with activity logs and join and exit timestamps.
- **Registration source tracking and notifications:** Registration origins are tracked automatically with UTM tracking built into email notifications, plus alerts when a webinar room nears or exceeds its capacity limit.
- **Data export and integrations:** One-click export of registrants, messages, and engagement with polls, handouts, and featured actions, through a centralized download center, plus merging of webinar data with a marketing automation platform or CRM.


**Limitations (as reported by users on**[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/demio/reviews) **):**


- **Streaming reliability:** The most frequently reported issue is streaming delays, audio problems, and disconnections during live sessions.
- **Browser and device dependence:** Users report microphone recognition failures and compatibility problems with certain browsers.
- **Data access after cancellation:** Reviewers report that registrant lists cannot be exported once a paid subscription ends.
- **Feature depth:** Several describe the platform as basic, with limited customization and integrations concentrated on the essentials.
- **Cost at higher tiers:** Premium features and larger room sizes are reported as restricted to higher-priced plans.

## Conclusion


Webinar software gives organizations a structured way to deliver live and on-demand virtual events while managing registration, engagement, follow-up, and reporting in one workflow. The right platform depends on audience size, event complexity, branding needs, interaction features, integrations, and analytics depth. Organizations should also compare streaming reliability, ease of setup, accessibility, security, and pricing to ensure the software can support both current event requirements and future growth.
